title: Pulse_Secure_Exploitation_Investigation_8c4
description: Investigate and respond to a potential Pulse Secure Exploitation malware incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity potentially related to the Pulse Secure Exploitation malware family. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is at IP address 192.168.50.5. Enter `start` to progress to the training levels.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is at IP address 192.168.50.5. Enter `start` to progress to the training levels.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Connections
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you've noticed unusual outbound connections from the target system. Investigate these connections to determine if they're malicious. The answer is a port number.
levels.solution: Check active network connections and listen ports on the target system. The suspicious port number used for the connections is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check active network connections and listen ports on the target system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `netstat -tuln` or `ss -tuln` to check active connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual ports that are listening or actively connected.

levels.title: Analyze Suspicious Service
levels.content: You've identified a suspicious service running on the target system. Analyze this service to understand its behavior and determine if it's related to the Pulse Secure Exploitation malware. The answer is a service name.
levels.solution: Examine the service configuration and related files to understand its purpose and behavior. The service name is `bkd.service` and its persistence mechanism is a systemd service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the service configuration and related files to understand its purpose and behavior.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual executables or scripts that the service might be running.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Evidence suggests that the attacker may be attempting to move laterally within the network. Investigate the target system to find any signs of lateral movement. The answer is a service name.
levels.solution: Check for any unusual file transfers or remote execution attempts. The service name or destination host used for lateral movement is `payload-transfer.service` and the destination host is `next-target`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for any unusual file transfers or remote execution attempts.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any network connections to other systems within the network.
